It is a Meccan surah.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

* *

The general discussion regarding what relates to the opening of this surah has already been presented at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah (tafsir, i.e., exegesis), namely that He, the Exalted, made this Qur'an a guidance, a healing and a mercy for the muhsinun (the doers of good), who are those who performed good deeds in following the Shari'ah (the sacred law). They established the obligatory prayer within its limits and its times, and what follows it of regular and irregular voluntary prayers; they gave the obligatory zakah (almsgiving) to those entitled to it; they maintained ties with their relatives and kin; and they were certain of the recompense in the Hereafter. So they longed for Allah's reward for these deeds, performing them not for show, nor desiring any recompense or thanks from people. Whoever does this, doing as they did, is among those of whom Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Those are upon guidance from their Lord﴾, that is, upon insight, clear evidence, and a plain and evident path, ﴿and those are the successful﴾, that is, in this world and the Hereafter.

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 31, verse 12:

The early scholars (al-salaf) differed about Luqman, peace be upon him: was he a prophet, or a righteous servant who was not a prophet? There are two opinions, and the majority hold the second.

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from al-A'mash, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: Luqman was an Abyssinian slave, a carpenter.

Qatadah narrated from 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr: I said to Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, "What has reached you about the matter of Luqman?" He said: "He was short, flat-nosed, from the Nubians."

Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari narrated from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: Luqman was from the blacks of Egypt, with thick lips. Allah gave him wisdom and withheld prophethood from him.

Al-Awza'i said, may Allah have mercy on him: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Harmalah told me, saying: A black man came to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab asking him something, and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said to him: "Do not grieve because you are black, for there were three of the best of people who were black: Bilal, Mihja' the freed slave of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, and Luqman the Wise, who was a black Nubian with thick lips" [Tafsir al-Tabari (21/43)].

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn WakI' narrated to us, from his father, from Abu al-Ashhab [in A: "al-Ash'ath"], from Khalid al-Rab'i, who said: Luqman was an Abyssinian slave, a carpenter. His master said to him, "Slaughter this sheep for us." He slaughtered it, and he said, "Take out the two best morsels from it." He took out the tongue and the heart. He remained for as long as Allah willed, then said, "Slaughter this sheep for us." He slaughtered it, and he said, "Take out the two worst morsels from it." He took out the tongue and the heart. His master said to him, "I ordered you to take out the two best morsels from it and you took them out, and I ordered you to take out the two worst morsels from it and you took them out." Luqman said, "There is nothing better than these two when they are good, and nothing worse than them when they are corrupt" [Tafsir al-Tabari (21/43)].

Shu'bah narrated from al-Hakam, from Mujahid: Luqman was a righteous servant, and he was not a prophet.

Al-A'mash said: Mujahid said, "Luqman was a black servant with large lips and cracked feet."

Hakkam ibn Salm narrated from Sa'id al-Zubaydi, from Mujahid: Luqman the Wise was an Abyssinian servant with thick lips and cracked feet, a judge over the Children of Israel.

Others mentioned that he was a judge over the Children of Israel in the time of Dawud, peace be upon him.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from 'Amr ibn Qays, who said: Luqman, peace be upon him, was a black servant with thick lips and cracked feet. A man came to him while he was in a gathering of people, teaching them, and said to him, "Are you not the one who used to graze the sheep with me in such-and-such a place?" He said, "Yes." The man said, "So what has brought you to what I see?" He said, "Truthfulness of speech, and silence about what does not concern me" [Tafsir al-Tabari (21/44)].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, from Safwan, from al-Walid, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, from Jabir, who said: Indeed Allah elevated Luqman the Wise by his wisdom, and a man who knew him before that saw him and said to him, "Are you not the servant of the sons of so-and-so, who used to graze [the sheep] yesterday?" He said, "Yes." He said, "So what has brought you to what I see?" He said, "The decree of Allah, the fulfilment of trust, truthfulness of speech, and leaving what does not concern me."

Among these reports, some explicitly deny that he was a prophet, and some imply it, because being a servant who has been subjected to slavery is incompatible with being a prophet, since prophets were sent among the noble lineages of their peoples. For this reason, the majority of the early scholars held that he was not a prophet. The view that he was a prophet is attributed only to Ikrimah, if the chain to him is sound: Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related it through WakI', from Isra'il, from Jabir, from Ikrimah, who said: "Luqman was a prophet." This Jabir is Ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, and he is weak. And Allah knows best.

'Abdullah ibn Wahb said: 'Abdullah ibn 'Ayyash al-Qitbani informed me, from 'Umar, the freed slave of Ghufrah, who said: A man stood before Luqman the Wise and said, "Are you Luqman? Are you the servant of the Banu al-Hisahas?" He said, "Yes." He said, "Are you the shepherd of the sheep?" He said, "Yes." He said, "Are you the black one?" He said, "As for my blackness, it is apparent. So what is it about my affair that impresses you?" He said, "People trample your carpet, crowd at your door, and are pleased with your words." He said, "O son of my brother, if you listen to what I tell you, you will be like that." Luqman said: "Lowering my gaze, restraining my tongue, the chastity of my food, guarding my private parts, speaking truthfully, fulfilling my promises, honouring my guest, protecting my neighbour, and leaving what does not concern me; that is what has brought me to what you see."

A strange report has come from Qatadah, transmitted by Ibn Abi Hatim, who said:

What Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated from Qatadah, concerning the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And We had certainly given Luqman wisdom﴾, that is, understanding of Islam, and he was not a prophet, and revelation did not come to him.

* *

His saying: ﴿And We had certainly given Luqman wisdom﴾ means understanding, knowledge and insight. ﴿Be grateful to Allah﴾ means: We commanded him to thank Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for what Allah gave him, granted him and bestowed upon him of favour, which He singled him out with above others of his kind and the people of his time.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever is grateful, it is only for [the benefit of] his own soul that he is grateful﴾, meaning: the benefit and reward of that return to the grateful themselves, like His saying the Exalted: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for their own souls that they prepare﴾ [Ar-Rum: 44].

* *

His saying: ﴿And whoever disbelieves - indeed, Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy﴾ means: He is free of need of the servants, and is not harmed by that, even if all the people of the earth disbelieved together, for He is the Self-Sufficient, Independent of all others. There is no god but Allah, and we worship none but Him.

And His saying: ﴿and his weaning is in two years﴾, meaning: his upbringing and his nursing after his birth, over two years, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And mothers nurse their children for two complete years, for whoever wishes to complete the nursing﴾ [al-Baqarah: 233].

For this reason He said: ﴿Give thanks to Me and to your parents; to Me is the final destination﴾, meaning: I will surely reward you for that with the fullest reward.

He stood, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: "I am the messenger of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to you: that you worship Allah and do not associate anything with Him, and that you obey me, I will not fail to do you good, and that the return is to Allah, and to Paradise or to the Fire, a permanent abode with no departure, and eternity with no death."

And His saying: ﴿But if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them﴾, meaning: if they are most eager that you follow them in their religion, then do not accept that from them, and let that not prevent you from accompanying them in this world with kindness, meaning: treating them well. ﴿And follow the way of those who turn back to Me﴾, meaning: the believers. ﴿Then to Me is your return, and I will inform you of what you used to do﴾.

When I saw that, I said: 'O mother, you know by Allah, if you had a hundred souls and they departed one soul after another, I would not abandon this religion of mine for anything. This passage contains advice that is highly beneficial, which Allah the Exalted related from Luqman the Wise, so that people may act upon it and follow it. He said: ﴿O my son, indeed it, if it should be the weight of a mustard seed﴾. That is, if the wrongdoing or the sin were the weight of a mustard seed [[addition from manuscripts T and A.]]. Some scholars permitted that the pronoun in His words ﴿indeed it﴾ be a pronoun of the matter and the story (ḍamīr al-sha'n wa'l-qiṣṣa), and on this basis they permitted the nominative case of ﴿weight﴾. The first view is the better.

As for His words ﴿Allah will bring it forth﴾, that is, Allah will produce it on the Day of Resurrection when He sets up the scales of justice, and He will recompense for it, good for good and evil for evil. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged in anything. And even if it should be the weight of a mustard seed, We would bring it forth. And sufficient are We as reckoners﴾ [al-Anbiyā’: 47]. And He the Exalted said: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it. And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 7–8]. Even if that atom were protected and hidden inside a solid rock, or absent and lost in the regions of the heavens or the earth, Allah would bring it forth, because nothing hidden is concealed from Him, and not even the weight of an atom escapes Him in the heavens or in the earth. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Subtle, Acquainted﴾, that is, Subtle in knowledge, so things are not hidden from Him however small, fine and minute they are, ﴿Acquainted﴾ with the crawling of the ant in the darkest night.

Some have claimed that what is meant by His words ﴿in a rock﴾ is a rock beneath the seven earths. This was mentioned by al-Suddi with his chain to that well-known transmission from Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud and a group of the Companions, if that is authentically established. It is also reported from 'Aṭiyyah al-'Awfi, Abu Malik, al-Thawri, al-Minhal ibn 'Amr and others. This, and Allah knows best, appears to be taken from the Isra'iliyyat (narratives derived from Jewish and Christian sources), which are neither confirmed nor denied. The apparent meaning, and Allah knows best, is that this grain, despite its smallness, even if it were inside a rock, Allah would make it appear and manifest it by His subtle knowledge, as the Imam Ahmad narrated:

Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, Ibn Lahī'ah narrated to us, Darrāj narrated to us, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who said: "If one of you were to work in a solid rock that has no door and no window, his deed would come out for the people, whatever it may be." [Musnad 3/28; al-Haythami graded it ḥasan in al-Majma' (10/225), but in its chain Ibn Lahī'ah narrates from Darrāj, and both are weak.]

Then he said: ﴿O my son, establish prayer﴾, that is, with its limits, obligations and times. ﴿And enjoin what is good and forbid what is wrong﴾, that is, according to your capacity and effort. ﴿And be patient over what has afflicted you﴾. He knew that one who enjoins good and forbids wrong will inevitably suffer harm from people, so he commanded him to be patient.

As for His words ﴿Indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination﴾, that is, indeed, patience over the harm of people is among the firm resolutions of affairs.

As for His words ﴿And do not turn your cheek [in contempt] toward people﴾, He says: do not turn your face away from people when you speak to them or they speak to you, out of contempt for them and arrogance over them. Rather, lower your side [in gentleness] and extend your face toward them, as came in the hadith: "Even if you meet your brother with a cheerful face. And beware of letting your garment trail, for it is of arrogance, and Allah does not love arrogance."

'Alī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah narrated from Ibn 'Abbās regarding His words ﴿And do not turn your cheek toward people﴾: he said, do not be arrogant so that you despise the servants of Allah and turn your face away from them when they speak to you. Similarly al-'Awfi and 'Ikrimah narrated from him.

Mālik narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam: ﴿And do not turn your cheek toward people﴾ means: do not speak while turning away. Similarly it is reported from Mujāhid, 'Ikrimah, Yazīd ibn al-Aṣamm, Abu al-Jawzā', Sa'īd ibn Jubayr, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Ibn Yazīd and others.

Ibrāhīm al-Nakha'ī said: it means affectation in speech (al-tashdīq fi'l-kalām).

The correct view is the first.

Ibn Jarīr said: The root of ṣa'ar is a disease that afflicts camels in their necks or heads, until their necks twist away from their heads. The arrogant man is likened to it. From this is the saying of 'Amr ibn Kulthūm al-Taghlibī:

"And we, when the tyrant turned his cheek [in arrogance], we straightened him from his inclination, and he straightened."

And Abu Ṭālib said in his poetry:

"And we were long ago not accepting injustice, when they bent their heads [in arrogance], we straightened them."

As for His words ﴿And do not walk upon the earth in arrogance﴾, that is, exultant, proud, haughty and obstinate. Do not do that, for Allah will hate you. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love everyone self-deluded and boastful﴾, that is, self-deluded and self-admiring, boastful over others. He the Exalted also said: ﴿And do not walk upon the earth in arrogance. Indeed, you will never tear the earth apart, nor will you reach the mountains in height﴾ [al-Isrā': 37]. The discussion of this has already preceded in its proper place.

The Ḥāfiẓ Abu al-Qāsim al-Ṭabarānī said: Muḥammad ibn 'Abd Allāh al-Ḥaḍramī narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn 'Imrān ibn Abī Laylā narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Laylā, from 'Īsā, from 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā [[in T: "And al-Ṭabarānī narrated with his chain."]], from Thābit ibn Qays ibn Shammās, who said: Arrogance was mentioned in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he spoke severely about it, saying: "Indeed Allah does not love everyone self-deluded and boastful." A man from the people said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I wash my garments and I am pleased with their whiteness, and I am pleased with the strap of my sandal and the handle of my whip." He said: "That is not arrogance. Arrogance is to reject the truth and to look down upon people." [al-Mu'jam al-Kabīr (2/69); there is a break in the chain between Ibn Abī Laylā and Thābit.]

He narrated it by another route with similar wording, and in it is a lengthy story, and the death of Thābit and his bequest after his death [al-Mu'jam al-Kabīr (2/70) through 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, from 'Aṭā', from the daughter of Thābit, with the story of her father; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (9/322): "I do not know the daughter of Thābit ibn Qays, but the rest of its narrators are narrators of the authentic (ṣaḥīḥ)."]

As for His words ﴿And be moderate in your pace﴾, that is, walk with a moderate gait, neither slow and lethargic, nor hasty and excessive, but with justice and a middle course between the two.

As for His words ﴿And lower your voice﴾, that is, do not exaggerate in speech, and do not raise your voice in what has no benefit. For this reason He the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, the most disagreeable of voices is the voice of donkeys﴾. Mujāhid and others said: indeed the ugliest of voices is the voice of donkeys, meaning that the extreme of one who raises his voice is that he is likened to donkeys in its loudness and elevation, and despite this it is hateful to Allah the Exalted. This comparison to donkeys in this matter requires its prohibition and the utmost censure, because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We have no evil likeness: the one who takes back his gift is like the dog that vomits and then returns to its vomit."

Al-Nasā'ī, while commenting on this verse, said: Qutaybah ibn Sa'īd narrated to us, al-Layth narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Rabī'ah, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "When you hear the crowing of roosters, ask Allah for His bounty, and when you hear the braying of donkeys, seek refuge in Allah from Satan, for indeed they have seen a devil."

It has been narrated by the rest of the group except Ibn Mājah, through several routes, from Ja'far ibn Rabī'ah with the same wording [al-Nasā'ī in al-Sunan al-Kubrā (11391); Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī no. 3301; Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim no. 2779; Sunan Abī Dāwūd no. 5102; Sunan al-Tirmidhī no. 3459]. In some wordings it has "at night." And Allah knows best.

These are very beneficial admonitions, and they are among the narratives of the Great Qur'an concerning Luqman the Wise. Much wisdom and admonition has been reported from him, so we shall mention from it a sample and a guide to that.

The Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubārak informed us, Sufyān informed us, Nahshal ibn Mujammi' al-Ḍabbī informed me, from Qaz'ah, from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with both of them, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) informed us, saying: "Indeed Luqman the Wise used to say: indeed when Allah is entrusted with something, He preserves it" [Musnad 2/87].

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: Abu Sa'īd al-Ashajj narrated to us, 'Īsā ibn Yūnus narrated to us, from al-Awzā'ī, from Mūsā ibn Sulaymān, from al-Qāsim [ibn Mukhaymirah narrates from Abu Mūsā al-Ash'arī] [[addition from A and al-Mustadrak.]] that the Messenger of Allah (ṣallā Allāhu 'alayhi wa-sallam) said: "Luqman said to his son while admonishing him: O my son, beware of face-covering, for it is a source of fear at night and a source of blame by day" [al-Ḥākim in al-Mustadrak (2/411) said: "This text has a supporting chain that is sound," and al-Dhahabī agreed].

And he said: My father narrated to us, 'Amr ibn 'Uthmān narrated to us, from Ḍamrah, al-Sarī ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, who said: Luqman said to his son: O my son, indeed wisdom has seated the poor in the gatherings of kings.

And he said: My father narrated to us, 'Abdah ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubārak informed us, 'Abd al-Raḥmān al-Mas'ūdī narrated to us [[in T: "Ibn Abī Ḥātim also narrated with his chain from al-Qāsim ibn Mukhaymirah."]], from 'Awn ibn 'Abd Allāh, who said: Luqman said to his son: O my son, when you come to a gathering of people, greet them with the arrow of Islam, that is, the greeting of peace, then sit in a corner of them, and do not speak until you see them speaking. If they discourse on the remembrance of Allah, then cast your arrow with them, and if they discourse on other than that, then turn away from them to others.

And my father narrated to us, 'Amr ibn 'Uthmān ibn Sa'īd ibn Kathīr ibn Dīnār narrated to us, Ḍamrah narrated to us [[in T: "And he also narrated."]], from Ḥafṣ ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Luqman placed a bag of mustard seeds beside himself, and he would admonish his son with an admonition and take out a mustard seed, until the mustard seeds ran out. Then he said: O my son, I have admonished you with an admonition that, if a mountain were admonished with it, it would split apart. He said: So his son split apart.

Abu al-Qāsim al-Ṭabarānī said: Yaḥyā ibn 'Abd al-Bāqī al-Miṣṣīṣī narrated to us, Aḥmad ibn 'Abd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥarrānī narrated to us, 'Uthmān ibn 'Abd al-Raḥmān al-Ṭarā'ifī narrated to us, Abyan [[in T, A, F, H: "Anas," corrected from al-Mu'jam al-Kabīr and the biographical works.]] ibn Sufyān al-Maqdisī narrated to us, from Khalīfah ibn Salām, from 'Aṭā' ibn Abī Rabāḥ [[in T: "And al-Ṭabarānī narrated with his chain."]], from Ibn 'Abbās who said: The Messenger of Allah (ṣallā Allāhu 'alayhi wa-sallam) said: "Take the Sudan (black people) as your companions, for three of them are among the masters of the people of Paradise: Luqman the Wise, al-Najāshī, and Bilāl the muezzin" [al-Mu'jam al-Kabīr (11/198); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (4/235): "In its chain is Abyan ibn Sufyān, who is weak."]

Abu al-Qāsim al-Ṭabarānī said: He meant the Abyssinians (al-Ḥabash).

**Section on Obscurity and Humility:** This relates to the counsel of Luqman (peace be upon him) to his son. The hadith scholar Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya compiled a separate book on this subject, and we mention its main points. He said:

Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn Musa al-Madani narrated to us, from Usama ibn Zayd, from Hafs ibn 'Ubaidullah ibn Anas ibn Malik: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "How many a dishevelled one clad in two worn garments, whose doors are shut against people, yet if he swears by Allah, Allah fulfils his oath." [[Also narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. 5054 (Majma' al-Bahrain), who said: "Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Halwani narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us," and then mentioned the same wording, and said: "No one narrated it from Hafs except Usama." It has a witness in Sahih Muslim, no. 2622, from the hadith of Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him). Note: this hadith is missing from the manuscript of Ibn Abi al-Dunya's al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul, as is the narration after it.]]

Then he narrated it from the hadith of Ja'far ibn Sulaiman, from Thabit and 'Ali ibn Zaid, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with the same wording, and he added: "Among them al-Bara' ibn Malik." [[Also narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan, no. 3854, through Sayyar, from Ja'far ibn Sulaiman with the same chain, and he said: "This is a hadith hasan sahih from this route."]]

[It is also narrated from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Blessed are the God-fearing rich who, when they are present, are not recognised, and when they are absent, they are not missed. They are lamps, free from every dark and defiling trial." [[Addition from manuscripts T and A.]]]

Abu Bakr ibn Sahl al-Tamimi said: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, Nafi' ibn Yazid narrated to us, from 'Ayyash ibn 'Abbas, from 'Isa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Zaid ibn Aslam, from his father, from 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), that he entered the mosque and found Mu'adh ibn Jabal weeping at the grave of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said to him: "What makes you weep, O Mu'adh?" He said: "A hadith I heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). I heard him say: 'Indeed, even a little showing-off is shirk. Allah loves the God-fearing, the hidden and the rich, who, when they are absent, are not missed, and when they are present, are not recognised. Their hearts are lamps of guidance; they are saved from every dark and gloomy trial.'" [[Al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul by Ibn Abi al-Dunya, no. 8.]]

Al-Walid ibn Shuja' narrated to us: 'Ussam ibn 'Ali narrated to us, from Humaid ibn 'Ata' al-A'raj, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "How many a one clad in two worn garments, who is looked down upon, if he swears by Allah, Allah fulfils his oath. If he says, 'O Allah, I ask You for Paradise,' He gives him Paradise, though He does not give him anything of this world." [[The hadith is missing from the manuscript of al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul. It is narrated by al-Daylami in Musnad al-Firdaws, no. 3246, through Ibn Abi al-Dunya.]]

He also said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Among my nation is one who, if he came to the door of one of you asking him for a dinar, a dirham or a fils, would not be given it; yet if he asked Allah for Paradise, He would give it to him. And if he asked Him for this world, He would not give it to him, and He would not withhold it from him out of contempt for him. He is one clad in two worn garments, who is looked down upon; if he swore by Allah, He would fulfil his oath." [[Al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul by Ibn Abi al-Dunya, no. 1. It is mursal (a hadith in which the Companion who heard it is omitted from the chain).]]

This is mursal through this route.

He also said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Ja'far ibn Sulaiman informed us, 'Awf narrated to us, who said: Abu Hurairah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Among the kings of Paradise is one who is dishevelled, dusty, clad in two worn garments, who is looked down upon. Such people, if they ask leave to enter upon the rulers, are not admitted, and if they propose marriage to women, they are not accepted, and if they speak, they are not listened to. The needs of one of them stick in his chest. If his light were divided among people on the Day of Resurrection, it would suffice them." [[Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated it in al-Awliya', no. 9, from al-Hasan, as a mursal, with similar wording. This hadith is missing from the manuscript of al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul.]]

He said: 'Umar ibn Shabbah recited to me, from Ibn 'A'ishah, who said: 'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said:

*Oh, how many a one clad in two worn garments in a dwelling,*
*Tomorrow, his carpets spread out and his cushions,*
*His rivers have flowed around his palace,*
*And it shone, and its gardens surrounded him.* [[Al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul by Ibn Abi al-Dunya, no. 5.]]

It is also narrated from the hadith of 'Ubaid Allah ibn Zahr, from 'Ali ibn Zaid, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, in a marfu' form (traced directly to the Prophet ﷺ): "Allah said: Among My closest friends in My sight is a believer who is lightly burdened, who has a share of prayer, who worships his Lord well, obeys Him in secret, and is obscure among people, not pointed at with fingers, if he is patient with that." He said: Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) struck his hand and said: "His death is hastened, his inheritance is small, and his mourners are few." [[Al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul, no. 13. Ibn Hibban said: "When 'Ubaid Allah ibn Zahr narrates from 'Ali ibn Yazid from al-Qasim, it is among what their hands have fabricated."]]

It is also narrated from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: The most beloved of Allah's servants to Allah are the strangers. It was asked: Who are the strangers? He said: Those who flee with their religion, who will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection with 'Isa ibn Maryam. [[Al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul, no. 16.]]

Al-Fudail ibn 'Iyad said: It has reached me that Allah, the Exalted, will say to the servant on the Day of Resurrection: "Did I not bestow favour upon you? Did I not give to you? Did I not conceal you? Did I not...? Did I not...? Did I not raise your remembrance?" Then al-Fudail said: "If you can avoid being known, then do so. What does it matter to you if you are not praised? What does it matter to you if you are blamed among people, yet praised by Allah?"

Ibn Muhairiz used to say: "O Allah, I ask You for an obscure remembrance."

Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad used to say: "O Allah, make me among the most exalted of Your creation in Your sight, make me among the lowliest of Your creation in my own soul, and among the average of Your creation in the eyes of people."

Then he said [i.e., Ibn Abi al-Dunya]: **Chapter on what has been reported about fame.**

Ahmad ibn 'Isa al-Misri narrated to us: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, from 'Umar ibn al-Harith and Ibn Lahi'ah, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Sinan ibn Sa'd, from Anas, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "It is enough evil for a person—except one whom Allah protects—that people point at him with their fingers, regarding his religion and his worldly life. Indeed, Allah does not look at your forms, but at your hearts and your deeds." [[Al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul, no. 30. In its chain is Sinan ibn Sa'd, who is weak.]]

A similar narration is reported from Ishaq ibn al-Bahlul, from Ibn Abi Fudaik, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Wahid al-Akhnasi, from 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Abi Kathir, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, in a marfu' form, similar to it. [[Al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul, no. 31. Al-Iraqi said: "It is not known from the hadith of Jabir; it is known only from the hadith of Abu Hurairah."]]

It is also reported, in a mursal form, from al-Hasan a similar narration. [[Al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul, no. 32.]] It was said to al-Hasan: "But one is pointed at with fingers?" He said: "What is meant is one who is pointed at regarding his religion for innovation, and regarding his worldly life for wickedness." [[Al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul, no. 33.]]

From 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: "Do not begin something in order to become famous, do not raise your figure so that you may be mentioned, learn and conceal, be silent and you will be safe; you will gladden the righteous and anger the wicked."

Ibrahim ibn Adham (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "He who loves fame has not been truthful to Allah."

Ayyub said: "No servant has been truthful to Allah unless he is pleased that his place is not noticed."

Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' said: "Whoever loves Allah loves that people do not know him."

Simak ibn Salamah said: "Beware of having many close friends."

Aban ibn 'Uthman said: "If you love that your religion remain sound for you, then reduce your acquaintances." Abu al-'Aliyah, when more than three people sat with him, would rise and leave them.

He said: 'Ali ibn al-Ja'd narrated to us, Shu'bah informed us, from 'Awf, from Abu Raja', who said: "Talhah saw a group walking with him and said: 'A fly of greed and a moth of the fire.'"

Ibn Idris said, from Harun ibn 'Anzarah [in manuscript A: "Harun ibn Abi 'Ushairah"], from Sulaim ibn Handhalah, who said: "While we were around my father, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab struck him with a whip and said: 'Indeed, it is a humiliation for the follower and a temptation for the one who is followed.'"

Ibn 'Awn said, from al-Hasan: "Ibn Mas'ud went out and people followed him. He said: 'By Allah, if you knew what I keep locked behind my door, not two of you would have followed me.'"

Hammad ibn Zaid said: "Whenever we passed by a gathering with Ayyub, and he greeted them, they returned the greeting very harshly, and that would grieve him."

'Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ma'mar: "Ayyub used to lengthen his shirt. He was asked about that and said: 'Fame in the past was in long shirts, and today it is in rolling them up.'" Once he had a pair of sandals made like the sandals of the Prophet (ﷺ), wore them for some days, then took them off and said: "I have not seen people wearing them."

Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: "Do not wear clothing that makes you famous among jurists, nor what makes foolish people look down on you."

al-Thawri said: "They used to dislike fine garments by which one becomes famous, at which people raise their eyes, and also shabby garments by which one is despised and his religion is belittled."

Khalid ibn Khidash narrated to us: Hammad narrated to us, from Abu Hasanah, companion of al-Ziyadi, who said: "We were with Abu Qilabah when a man entered upon him wearing a rough cloak. He said: 'Beware of this braying donkey.'"

Al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "Some people have placed arrogance in their hearts and humility in their clothes. The owner of a cloak with his cloak is more wondrous than the owner of a striped garment with his garment. What is wrong with them? They have lost their sense of what is right."

It is reported in some reports that Musa (peace be upon him) said to the Children of Israel: "What is wrong with you, that you come to me wearing the garments of monks, while your hearts are the hearts of wolves? Wear the garments of kings and soften your hearts with fear."

**Section on Good Character**

Abu al-Tayyah said, from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him): "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was among the best of people in character." [[Al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul, no. 163.]]

And from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Umar: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, which of the believers is most excellent?" He said: "The best of them in character." [[Al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul, no. 164.]]

From Nuh ibn 'Abbad, from Thabit, from Anas, in a marfu' form: "A servant may reach, through his good character, the ranks of the Hereafter and the nobility of stations, even though he is weak in worship. And he may reach, through his bad character, the depths of Hell, even though he is an worshipper." [[Al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul, no. 168.]] From Sinan ibn Harun, from Humaid, from Anas, in a marfu' form: "Good character has gone with the good of this world and the Hereafter." [[Al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul, no. 169.]] From 'A'ishah, in a marfu' form: "A servant may reach, through his good character, the rank of one who stands in prayer at night and fasts by day." [[Al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul, no. 166.]]

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Abu Muslim 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yunus narrated to me, 'Abdullah ibn Idris narrated to us, my father and my paternal uncle informed me, from my grandfather, from Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about what most admits people into Paradise, and he said: "The fear of Allah and good character." He was asked about what most admits people into the Fire, and he said: "The two hollows: the mouth and the private parts." [[Al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul, no. 170.]]

Usamah ibn Shuraik said: "I was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when the Bedouins came to him from every place and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the best thing a person can be given?' He said: 'Good character.'" [[Al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul, no. 171.]]

Ya'la ibn Mamlak said, from Umm al-Darda', from Abu al-Darda', who traced it back (to the Prophet ﷺ): "Nothing is heavier in the Scale than good character." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 172]. Similarly, 'Ata' narrated it from Umm al-Darda', with the same wording. [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 173].

And from Masruq, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, raised to the Prophet: "Indeed, among the best of you are those with the best character." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 174].

'Abdullah ibn Abi Badr narrated to us: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abi Sarah, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, Allah gives the servant reward for good character just as He gives the one who strives in the way of Allah; the reward comes to him morning and evening." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 176].

And from Makhul, from Abu Tha'laba, raised to the Prophet: "Indeed, the most beloved of you to me and the nearest of you to me in gathering are those with the best character. And indeed, the most hated of you to me and the farthest of you from me in the abode in Paradise are those with the worst character: the chatterers, the bombastic, and the pretentious (al-mutafayhiqun)." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 177].

And from Abu Uways, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, raised to the Prophet: "Shall I not inform you of the most perfect of you in faith? Those with the best character, who are gentle and easy to approach, who are loved and who love." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 178].

Al-Laith said, from Yazid ibn 'Abdullah ibn Usama, from Bakr ibn Abi al-Furat, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah does not beautify a man's form and character and then have the Fire consume him." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 180].

And from 'Abdullah ibn Ghalib al-Haddani, from Abu Sa'id, raised to the Prophet: "Two qualities do not combine in a believer: stinginess and bad character." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 182]. Maymun ibn Mihran said, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "There is no sin greater before Allah than bad character, because its possessor does not emerge from one sin except that he falls into another." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 183].

'Ali ibn al-Ja'd narrated to us: Abu al-Mughira al-Ahmasi narrated to us: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from a man of Quraysh, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is no sin greater before Allah than bad character. Indeed, good character melts sins as the sun melts ice, and bad character corrupts deeds as vinegar corrupts honey." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 184].

And 'Abdullah ibn Idris said, from his father, from his grandfather, from Abu Hurayra, raised to the Prophet: "Indeed, you cannot satisfy people with your wealth, but they can be satisfied by you through a cheerful face and good character." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 190].

Muhammad ibn Sirin said: Good character is a help in religion.

Section on the Condemnation of Arrogance (al-Kibr)

'Alqama said, from Ibn Mas'ud, raised: "No one who has in his heart the weight of a mustard seed of arrogance will enter Paradise, and no one who has in his heart the weight of a mustard seed of faith will enter the Fire." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 192].

Ibrahim ibn Abi 'Abla said, from Abu Salama, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, raised: "Whoever has in his heart the weight of an atom of arrogance, Allah will throw him on his face into the Fire." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 196].

Ishaq ibn Isma'il narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from 'Umar ibn Rashid, from Iyas ibn Salama, from his father, raised: "A man will continue to exalt himself until he is recorded with Allah among the tyrants, and then he will suffer what they suffered of punishment." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 198].

Malik ibn Dinar said: Sulayman ibn Dawud, peace be upon them both, once rode the carpet with two hundred thousand of mankind and two hundred thousand of the jinn. It was raised until he heard the glorification of the angels in the sky, then it was lowered until his foot touched the water of the sea, and they heard a voice: "If there were in the heart of your companion the weight of an atom of arrogance, he would be swallowed up by the earth even further than he was raised."

Abu Khaythama narrated to us: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salama, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: Abu Bakr used to address us and mention the beginning of the creation of man, to the extent that one of us would disgust himself, saying: "He came out of the passage of urine twice." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 200].

Al-Sha'bi said: Whoever kills two people is a tyrant (jabbar). Then he recited: ﴿Do you want to kill me as you killed a soul yesterday? You only want to be a tyrant in the land.﴾ [al-Qasas: 19]. Al-Hasan said: "How strange is the son of Adam! He washes filth with his hand twice a day, then he is arrogant! He contends with the Tyrant of the heavens." He said: Khalid ibn Khidash narrated to us: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn al-Hasan, from al-Dahhak ibn Sufyan, and he mentioned the hadith, which struck the example of this world with what comes out of the son of Adam. [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 210].

Al-Hasan said, from Yahya, from his father, who said: Indeed, the food of the son of Adam is a parable for this world, even if it is sweetened and salted.

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn 'Ali, from the descendants of 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Nothing of arrogance enters a man's heart except that it reduces his intellect to the extent of that.

Yunus ibn 'Ubayd said: There is no arrogance with prostration, and there is no hypocrisy with monotheism.

Tawus saw 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz walking with a swaggering gait, and that was before he became caliph. Tawus poked him in the side with his finger and said: "Is this the way of one who has filth in his belly?" 'Umar, as one apologizing to him, said: "O uncle, every limb of mine was beaten into this gait until I learned it."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya said: The Banu Umayya used to beat their children until they learned this gait.

Section on Strutting (al-Ikhtiyal)

From Abu Layla, from Ibn Buraydah, from his father, raised: "Whoever drags his garment out of arrogance, Allah will not look at him." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 238].

It was also narrated from Ishaq ibn Isma'il, from Sufyan, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ibn 'Umar, raised, similarly [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 239]. Muhammad ibn Bakkar narrated to us: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad narrated to us, from his father, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayra, raised: "Allah will not look on the Day of Resurrection at the one who drags his izar." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 232]. And: "While a man was strutting in his two cloaks, admiring himself, Allah caused the earth to swallow him, and he will keep sinking into it until the Day of Resurrection." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 233].

Al-Zuhri narrated from Salim, from his father: "While a man ..." to its end. [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 234].

This passage contains advice that is highly beneficial, which Allah the Exalted related from Luqman the Wise, so that people may act upon it and follow it. He said: ﴿O my son, indeed it, if it should be the weight of a mustard seed﴾. That is, if the wrongdoing or the sin were the weight of a mustard seed [[addition from manuscripts T and A.]]. Some scholars permitted that the pronoun in His words ﴿indeed it﴾ be a pronoun of the matter and the story (ḍamīr al-sha'n wa'l-qiṣṣa), and on this basis they permitted the nominative case of ﴿weight﴾. The first view is the better.

As for His words ﴿Allah will bring it forth﴾, that is, Allah will produce it on the Day of Resurrection when He sets up the scales of justice, and He will recompense for it, good for good and evil for evil. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged in anything. And even if it should be the weight of a mustard seed, We would bring it forth. And sufficient are We as reckoners﴾ [al-Anbiyā’: 47]. And He the Exalted said: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it. And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 7–8]. Even if that atom were protected and hidden inside a solid rock, or absent and lost in the regions of the heavens or the earth, Allah would bring it forth, because nothing hidden is concealed from Him, and not even the weight of an atom escapes Him in the heavens or in the earth. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Subtle, Acquainted﴾, that is, Subtle in knowledge, so things are not hidden from Him however small, fine and minute they are, ﴿Acquainted﴾ with the crawling of the ant in the darkest night.

Some have claimed that what is meant by His words ﴿in a rock﴾ is a rock beneath the seven earths. This was mentioned by al-Suddi with his chain to that well-known transmission from Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud and a group of the Companions, if that is authentically established. It is also reported from 'Aṭiyyah al-'Awfi, Abu Malik, al-Thawri, al-Minhal ibn 'Amr and others. This, and Allah knows best, appears to be taken from the Isra'iliyyat (narratives derived from Jewish and Christian sources), which are neither confirmed nor denied. The apparent meaning, and Allah knows best, is that this grain, despite its smallness, even if it were inside a rock, Allah would make it appear and manifest it by His subtle knowledge, as the Imam Ahmad narrated:

Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, Ibn Lahī'ah narrated to us, Darrāj narrated to us, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who said: "If one of you were to work in a solid rock that has no door and no window, his deed would come out for the people, whatever it may be." [Musnad 3/28; al-Haythami graded it ḥasan in al-Majma' (10/225), but in its chain Ibn Lahī'ah narrates from Darrāj, and both are weak.]

Then he said: ﴿O my son, establish prayer﴾, that is, with its limits, obligations and times. ﴿And enjoin what is good and forbid what is wrong﴾, that is, according to your capacity and effort. ﴿And be patient over what has afflicted you﴾. He knew that one who enjoins good and forbids wrong will inevitably suffer harm from people, so he commanded him to be patient.

As for His words ﴿Indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination﴾, that is, indeed, patience over the harm of people is among the firm resolutions of affairs.

As for His words ﴿And do not turn your cheek [in contempt] toward people﴾, He says: do not turn your face away from people when you speak to them or they speak to you, out of contempt for them and arrogance over them. Rather, lower your side [in gentleness] and extend your face toward them, as came in the hadith: "Even if you meet your brother with a cheerful face. And beware of letting your garment trail, for it is of arrogance, and Allah does not love arrogance."

'Alī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah narrated from Ibn 'Abbās regarding His words ﴿And do not turn your cheek toward people﴾: he said, do not be arrogant so that you despise the servants of Allah and turn your face away from them when they speak to you. Similarly al-'Awfi and 'Ikrimah narrated from him.

Mālik narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam: ﴿And do not turn your cheek toward people﴾ means: do not speak while turning away. Similarly it is reported from Mujāhid, 'Ikrimah, Yazīd ibn al-Aṣamm, Abu al-Jawzā', Sa'īd ibn Jubayr, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Ibn Yazīd and others.

Ibrāhīm al-Nakha'ī said: it means affectation in speech (al-tashdīq fi'l-kalām).

The correct view is the first.

Ibn Jarīr said: The root of ṣa'ar is a disease that afflicts camels in their necks or heads, until their necks twist away from their heads. The arrogant man is likened to it. From this is the saying of 'Amr ibn Kulthūm al-Taghlibī:

"And we, when the tyrant turned his cheek [in arrogance], we straightened him from his inclination, and he straightened."

And Abu Ṭālib said in his poetry:

"And we were long ago not accepting injustice, when they bent their heads [in arrogance], we straightened them."

As for His words ﴿And do not walk upon the earth in arrogance﴾, that is, exultant, proud, haughty and obstinate. Do not do that, for Allah will hate you. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love everyone self-deluded and boastful﴾, that is, self-deluded and self-admiring, boastful over others. He the Exalted also said: ﴿And do not walk upon the earth in arrogance. Indeed, you will never tear the earth apart, nor will you reach the mountains in height﴾ [al-Isrā': 37]. The discussion of this has already preceded in its proper place.

The Ḥāfiẓ Abu al-Qāsim al-Ṭabarānī said: Muḥammad ibn 'Abd Allāh al-Ḥaḍramī narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn 'Imrān ibn Abī Laylā narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Laylā, from 'Īsā, from 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā [[in T: "And al-Ṭabarānī narrated with his chain."]], from Thābit ibn Qays ibn Shammās, who said: Arrogance was mentioned in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he spoke severely about it, saying: "Indeed Allah does not love everyone self-deluded and boastful." A man from the people said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I wash my garments and I am pleased with their whiteness, and I am pleased with the strap of my sandal and the handle of my whip." He said: "That is not arrogance. Arrogance is to reject the truth and to look down upon people." [al-Mu'jam al-Kabīr (2/69); there is a break in the chain between Ibn Abī Laylā and Thābit.]

He narrated it by another route with similar wording, and in it is a lengthy story, and the death of Thābit and his bequest after his death [al-Mu'jam al-Kabīr (2/70) through 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, from 'Aṭā', from the daughter of Thābit, with the story of her father; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (9/322): "I do not know the daughter of Thābit ibn Qays, but the rest of its narrators are narrators of the authentic (ṣaḥīḥ)."]

As for His words ﴿And be moderate in your pace﴾, that is, walk with a moderate gait, neither slow and lethargic, nor hasty and excessive, but with justice and a middle course between the two.

As for His words ﴿And lower your voice﴾, that is, do not exaggerate in speech, and do not raise your voice in what has no benefit. For this reason He the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, the most disagreeable of voices is the voice of donkeys﴾. Mujāhid and others said: indeed the ugliest of voices is the voice of donkeys, meaning that the extreme of one who raises his voice is that he is likened to donkeys in its loudness and elevation, and despite this it is hateful to Allah the Exalted. This comparison to donkeys in this matter requires its prohibition and the utmost censure, because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We have no evil likeness: the one who takes back his gift is like the dog that vomits and then returns to its vomit."

Al-Nasā'ī, while commenting on this verse, said: Qutaybah ibn Sa'īd narrated to us, al-Layth narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Rabī'ah, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "When you hear the crowing of roosters, ask Allah for His bounty, and when you hear the braying of donkeys, seek refuge in Allah from Satan, for indeed they have seen a devil."

It has been narrated by the rest of the group except Ibn Mājah, through several routes, from Ja'far ibn Rabī'ah with the same wording [al-Nasā'ī in al-Sunan al-Kubrā (11391); Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī no. 3301; Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim no. 2779; Sunan Abī Dāwūd no. 5102; Sunan al-Tirmidhī no. 3459]. In some wordings it has "at night." And Allah knows best.

These are very beneficial admonitions, and they are among the narratives of the Great Qur'an concerning Luqman the Wise. Much wisdom and admonition has been reported from him, so we shall mention from it a sample and a guide to that.

The Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubārak informed us, Sufyān informed us, Nahshal ibn Mujammi' al-Ḍabbī informed me, from Qaz'ah, from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with both of them, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) informed us, saying: "Indeed Luqman the Wise used to say: indeed when Allah is entrusted with something, He preserves it" [Musnad 2/87].

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: Abu Sa'īd al-Ashajj narrated to us, 'Īsā ibn Yūnus narrated to us, from al-Awzā'ī, from Mūsā ibn Sulaymān, from al-Qāsim [ibn Mukhaymirah narrates from Abu Mūsā al-Ash'arī] [[addition from A and al-Mustadrak.]] that the Messenger of Allah (ṣallā Allāhu 'alayhi wa-sallam) said: "Luqman said to his son while admonishing him: O my son, beware of face-covering, for it is a source of fear at night and a source of blame by day" [al-Ḥākim in al-Mustadrak (2/411) said: "This text has a supporting chain that is sound," and al-Dhahabī agreed].

And he said: My father narrated to us, 'Amr ibn 'Uthmān narrated to us, from Ḍamrah, al-Sarī ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, who said: Luqman said to his son: O my son, indeed wisdom has seated the poor in the gatherings of kings.

And he said: My father narrated to us, 'Abdah ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubārak informed us, 'Abd al-Raḥmān al-Mas'ūdī narrated to us [[in T: "Ibn Abī Ḥātim also narrated with his chain from al-Qāsim ibn Mukhaymirah."]], from 'Awn ibn 'Abd Allāh, who said: Luqman said to his son: O my son, when you come to a gathering of people, greet them with the arrow of Islam, that is, the greeting of peace, then sit in a corner of them, and do not speak until you see them speaking. If they discourse on the remembrance of Allah, then cast your arrow with them, and if they discourse on other than that, then turn away from them to others.

And my father narrated to us, 'Amr ibn 'Uthmān ibn Sa'īd ibn Kathīr ibn Dīnār narrated to us, Ḍamrah narrated to us [[in T: "And he also narrated."]], from Ḥafṣ ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Luqman placed a bag of mustard seeds beside himself, and he would admonish his son with an admonition and take out a mustard seed, until the mustard seeds ran out. Then he said: O my son, I have admonished you with an admonition that, if a mountain were admonished with it, it would split apart. He said: So his son split apart.

Abu al-Qāsim al-Ṭabarānī said: Yaḥyā ibn 'Abd al-Bāqī al-Miṣṣīṣī narrated to us, Aḥmad ibn 'Abd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥarrānī narrated to us, 'Uthmān ibn 'Abd al-Raḥmān al-Ṭarā'ifī narrated to us, Abyan [[in T, A, F, H: "Anas," corrected from al-Mu'jam al-Kabīr and the biographical works.]] ibn Sufyān al-Maqdisī narrated to us, from Khalīfah ibn Salām, from 'Aṭā' ibn Abī Rabāḥ [[in T: "And al-Ṭabarānī narrated with his chain."]], from Ibn 'Abbās who said: The Messenger of Allah (ṣallā Allāhu 'alayhi wa-sallam) said: "Take the Sudan (black people) as your companions, for three of them are among the masters of the people of Paradise: Luqman the Wise, al-Najāshī, and Bilāl the muezzin" [al-Mu'jam al-Kabīr (11/198); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (4/235): "In its chain is Abyan ibn Sufyān, who is weak."]

Abu al-Qāsim al-Ṭabarānī said: He meant the Abyssinians (al-Ḥabash).

**Section on Obscurity and Humility:** This relates to the counsel of Luqman (peace be upon him) to his son. The hadith scholar Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya compiled a separate book on this subject, and we mention its main points. He said:

Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn Musa al-Madani narrated to us, from Usama ibn Zayd, from Hafs ibn 'Ubaidullah ibn Anas ibn Malik: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "How many a dishevelled one clad in two worn garments, whose doors are shut against people, yet if he swears by Allah, Allah fulfils his oath." [[Also narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. 5054 (Majma' al-Bahrain), who said: "Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Halwani narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us," and then mentioned the same wording, and said: "No one narrated it from Hafs except Usama." It has a witness in Sahih Muslim, no. 2622, from the hadith of Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him). Note: this hadith is missing from the manuscript of Ibn Abi al-Dunya's al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul, as is the narration after it.]]

Then he narrated it from the hadith of Ja'far ibn Sulaiman, from Thabit and 'Ali ibn Zaid, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with the same wording, and he added: "Among them al-Bara' ibn Malik." [[Also narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan, no. 3854, through Sayyar, from Ja'far ibn Sulaiman with the same chain, and he said: "This is a hadith hasan sahih from this route."]]

[It is also narrated from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Blessed are the God-fearing rich who, when they are present, are not recognised, and when they are absent, they are not missed. They are lamps, free from every dark and defiling trial." [[Addition from manuscripts T and A.]]]

Abu Bakr ibn Sahl al-Tamimi said: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, Nafi' ibn Yazid narrated to us, from 'Ayyash ibn 'Abbas, from 'Isa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Zaid ibn Aslam, from his father, from 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), that he entered the mosque and found Mu'adh ibn Jabal weeping at the grave of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said to him: "What makes you weep, O Mu'adh?" He said: "A hadith I heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). I heard him say: 'Indeed, even a little showing-off is shirk. Allah loves the God-fearing, the hidden and the rich, who, when they are absent, are not missed, and when they are present, are not recognised. Their hearts are lamps of guidance; they are saved from every dark and gloomy trial.'" [[Al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul by Ibn Abi al-Dunya, no. 8.]]

Al-Walid ibn Shuja' narrated to us: 'Ussam ibn 'Ali narrated to us, from Humaid ibn 'Ata' al-A'raj, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "How many a one clad in two worn garments, who is looked down upon, if he swears by Allah, Allah fulfils his oath. If he says, 'O Allah, I ask You for Paradise,' He gives him Paradise, though He does not give him anything of this world." [[The hadith is missing from the manuscript of al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul. It is narrated by al-Daylami in Musnad al-Firdaws, no. 3246, through Ibn Abi al-Dunya.]]

He also said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Among my nation is one who, if he came to the door of one of you asking him for a dinar, a dirham or a fils, would not be given it; yet if he asked Allah for Paradise, He would give it to him. And if he asked Him for this world, He would not give it to him, and He would not withhold it from him out of contempt for him. He is one clad in two worn garments, who is looked down upon; if he swore by Allah, He would fulfil his oath." [[Al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul by Ibn Abi al-Dunya, no. 1. It is mursal (a hadith in which the Companion who heard it is omitted from the chain).]]

This is mursal through this route.

He also said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Ja'far ibn Sulaiman informed us, 'Awf narrated to us, who said: Abu Hurairah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Among the kings of Paradise is one who is dishevelled, dusty, clad in two worn garments, who is looked down upon. Such people, if they ask leave to enter upon the rulers, are not admitted, and if they propose marriage to women, they are not accepted, and if they speak, they are not listened to. The needs of one of them stick in his chest. If his light were divided among people on the Day of Resurrection, it would suffice them." [[Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated it in al-Awliya', no. 9, from al-Hasan, as a mursal, with similar wording. This hadith is missing from the manuscript of al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul.]]

He said: 'Umar ibn Shabbah recited to me, from Ibn 'A'ishah, who said: 'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said:

*Oh, how many a one clad in two worn garments in a dwelling,*
*Tomorrow, his carpets spread out and his cushions,*
*His rivers have flowed around his palace,*
*And it shone, and its gardens surrounded him.* [[Al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul by Ibn Abi al-Dunya, no. 5.]]

It is also narrated from the hadith of 'Ubaid Allah ibn Zahr, from 'Ali ibn Zaid, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, in a marfu' form (traced directly to the Prophet ﷺ): "Allah said: Among My closest friends in My sight is a believer who is lightly burdened, who has a share of prayer, who worships his Lord well, obeys Him in secret, and is obscure among people, not pointed at with fingers, if he is patient with that." He said: Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) struck his hand and said: "His death is hastened, his inheritance is small, and his mourners are few." [[Al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul, no. 13. Ibn Hibban said: "When 'Ubaid Allah ibn Zahr narrates from 'Ali ibn Yazid from al-Qasim, it is among what their hands have fabricated."]]

It is also narrated from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: The most beloved of Allah's servants to Allah are the strangers. It was asked: Who are the strangers? He said: Those who flee with their religion, who will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection with 'Isa ibn Maryam. [[Al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul, no. 16.]]

Al-Fudail ibn 'Iyad said: It has reached me that Allah, the Exalted, will say to the servant on the Day of Resurrection: "Did I not bestow favour upon you? Did I not give to you? Did I not conceal you? Did I not...? Did I not...? Did I not raise your remembrance?" Then al-Fudail said: "If you can avoid being known, then do so. What does it matter to you if you are not praised? What does it matter to you if you are blamed among people, yet praised by Allah?"

Ibn Muhairiz used to say: "O Allah, I ask You for an obscure remembrance."

Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad used to say: "O Allah, make me among the most exalted of Your creation in Your sight, make me among the lowliest of Your creation in my own soul, and among the average of Your creation in the eyes of people."

Then he said [i.e., Ibn Abi al-Dunya]: **Chapter on what has been reported about fame.**

Ahmad ibn 'Isa al-Misri narrated to us: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, from 'Umar ibn al-Harith and Ibn Lahi'ah, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Sinan ibn Sa'd, from Anas, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "It is enough evil for a person—except one whom Allah protects—that people point at him with their fingers, regarding his religion and his worldly life. Indeed, Allah does not look at your forms, but at your hearts and your deeds." [[Al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul, no. 30. In its chain is Sinan ibn Sa'd, who is weak.]]

A similar narration is reported from Ishaq ibn al-Bahlul, from Ibn Abi Fudaik, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Wahid al-Akhnasi, from 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Abi Kathir, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, in a marfu' form, similar to it. [[Al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul, no. 31. Al-Iraqi said: "It is not known from the hadith of Jabir; it is known only from the hadith of Abu Hurairah."]]

It is also reported, in a mursal form, from al-Hasan a similar narration. [[Al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul, no. 32.]] It was said to al-Hasan: "But one is pointed at with fingers?" He said: "What is meant is one who is pointed at regarding his religion for innovation, and regarding his worldly life for wickedness." [[Al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul, no. 33.]]

From 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: "Do not begin something in order to become famous, do not raise your figure so that you may be mentioned, learn and conceal, be silent and you will be safe; you will gladden the righteous and anger the wicked."

Ibrahim ibn Adham (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "He who loves fame has not been truthful to Allah."

Ayyub said: "No servant has been truthful to Allah unless he is pleased that his place is not noticed."

Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' said: "Whoever loves Allah loves that people do not know him."

Simak ibn Salamah said: "Beware of having many close friends."

Aban ibn 'Uthman said: "If you love that your religion remain sound for you, then reduce your acquaintances." Abu al-'Aliyah, when more than three people sat with him, would rise and leave them.

He said: 'Ali ibn al-Ja'd narrated to us, Shu'bah informed us, from 'Awf, from Abu Raja', who said: "Talhah saw a group walking with him and said: 'A fly of greed and a moth of the fire.'"

Ibn Idris said, from Harun ibn 'Anzarah [in manuscript A: "Harun ibn Abi 'Ushairah"], from Sulaim ibn Handhalah, who said: "While we were around my father, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab struck him with a whip and said: 'Indeed, it is a humiliation for the follower and a temptation for the one who is followed.'"

Ibn 'Awn said, from al-Hasan: "Ibn Mas'ud went out and people followed him. He said: 'By Allah, if you knew what I keep locked behind my door, not two of you would have followed me.'"

Hammad ibn Zaid said: "Whenever we passed by a gathering with Ayyub, and he greeted them, they returned the greeting very harshly, and that would grieve him."

'Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ma'mar: "Ayyub used to lengthen his shirt. He was asked about that and said: 'Fame in the past was in long shirts, and today it is in rolling them up.'" Once he had a pair of sandals made like the sandals of the Prophet (ﷺ), wore them for some days, then took them off and said: "I have not seen people wearing them."

Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: "Do not wear clothing that makes you famous among jurists, nor what makes foolish people look down on you."

al-Thawri said: "They used to dislike fine garments by which one becomes famous, at which people raise their eyes, and also shabby garments by which one is despised and his religion is belittled."

Khalid ibn Khidash narrated to us: Hammad narrated to us, from Abu Hasanah, companion of al-Ziyadi, who said: "We were with Abu Qilabah when a man entered upon him wearing a rough cloak. He said: 'Beware of this braying donkey.'"

Al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "Some people have placed arrogance in their hearts and humility in their clothes. The owner of a cloak with his cloak is more wondrous than the owner of a striped garment with his garment. What is wrong with them? They have lost their sense of what is right."

It is reported in some reports that Musa (peace be upon him) said to the Children of Israel: "What is wrong with you, that you come to me wearing the garments of monks, while your hearts are the hearts of wolves? Wear the garments of kings and soften your hearts with fear."

**Section on Good Character**

Abu al-Tayyah said, from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him): "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was among the best of people in character." [[Al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul, no. 163.]]

And from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Umar: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, which of the believers is most excellent?" He said: "The best of them in character." [[Al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul, no. 164.]]

From Nuh ibn 'Abbad, from Thabit, from Anas, in a marfu' form: "A servant may reach, through his good character, the ranks of the Hereafter and the nobility of stations, even though he is weak in worship. And he may reach, through his bad character, the depths of Hell, even though he is an worshipper." [[Al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul, no. 168.]] From Sinan ibn Harun, from Humaid, from Anas, in a marfu' form: "Good character has gone with the good of this world and the Hereafter." [[Al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul, no. 169.]] From 'A'ishah, in a marfu' form: "A servant may reach, through his good character, the rank of one who stands in prayer at night and fasts by day." [[Al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul, no. 166.]]

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Abu Muslim 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yunus narrated to me, 'Abdullah ibn Idris narrated to us, my father and my paternal uncle informed me, from my grandfather, from Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about what most admits people into Paradise, and he said: "The fear of Allah and good character." He was asked about what most admits people into the Fire, and he said: "The two hollows: the mouth and the private parts." [[Al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul, no. 170.]]

Usamah ibn Shuraik said: "I was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when the Bedouins came to him from every place and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the best thing a person can be given?' He said: 'Good character.'" [[Al-Tawadu' wa'l-Khumul, no. 171.]]

Ya'la ibn Mamlak said, from Umm al-Darda', from Abu al-Darda', who traced it back (to the Prophet ﷺ): "Nothing is heavier in the Scale than good character." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 172]. Similarly, 'Ata' narrated it from Umm al-Darda', with the same wording. [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 173].

And from Masruq, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, raised to the Prophet: "Indeed, among the best of you are those with the best character." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 174].

'Abdullah ibn Abi Badr narrated to us: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abi Sarah, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, Allah gives the servant reward for good character just as He gives the one who strives in the way of Allah; the reward comes to him morning and evening." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 176].

And from Makhul, from Abu Tha'laba, raised to the Prophet: "Indeed, the most beloved of you to me and the nearest of you to me in gathering are those with the best character. And indeed, the most hated of you to me and the farthest of you from me in the abode in Paradise are those with the worst character: the chatterers, the bombastic, and the pretentious (al-mutafayhiqun)." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 177].

And from Abu Uways, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, raised to the Prophet: "Shall I not inform you of the most perfect of you in faith? Those with the best character, who are gentle and easy to approach, who are loved and who love." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 178].

Al-Laith said, from Yazid ibn 'Abdullah ibn Usama, from Bakr ibn Abi al-Furat, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah does not beautify a man's form and character and then have the Fire consume him." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 180].

And from 'Abdullah ibn Ghalib al-Haddani, from Abu Sa'id, raised to the Prophet: "Two qualities do not combine in a believer: stinginess and bad character." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 182]. Maymun ibn Mihran said, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "There is no sin greater before Allah than bad character, because its possessor does not emerge from one sin except that he falls into another." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 183].

'Ali ibn al-Ja'd narrated to us: Abu al-Mughira al-Ahmasi narrated to us: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from a man of Quraysh, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is no sin greater before Allah than bad character. Indeed, good character melts sins as the sun melts ice, and bad character corrupts deeds as vinegar corrupts honey." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 184].

And 'Abdullah ibn Idris said, from his father, from his grandfather, from Abu Hurayra, raised to the Prophet: "Indeed, you cannot satisfy people with your wealth, but they can be satisfied by you through a cheerful face and good character." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 190].

Muhammad ibn Sirin said: Good character is a help in religion.

Section on the Condemnation of Arrogance (al-Kibr)

'Alqama said, from Ibn Mas'ud, raised: "No one who has in his heart the weight of a mustard seed of arrogance will enter Paradise, and no one who has in his heart the weight of a mustard seed of faith will enter the Fire." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 192].

Ibrahim ibn Abi 'Abla said, from Abu Salama, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, raised: "Whoever has in his heart the weight of an atom of arrogance, Allah will throw him on his face into the Fire." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 196].

Ishaq ibn Isma'il narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from 'Umar ibn Rashid, from Iyas ibn Salama, from his father, raised: "A man will continue to exalt himself until he is recorded with Allah among the tyrants, and then he will suffer what they suffered of punishment." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 198].

Malik ibn Dinar said: Sulayman ibn Dawud, peace be upon them both, once rode the carpet with two hundred thousand of mankind and two hundred thousand of the jinn. It was raised until he heard the glorification of the angels in the sky, then it was lowered until his foot touched the water of the sea, and they heard a voice: "If there were in the heart of your companion the weight of an atom of arrogance, he would be swallowed up by the earth even further than he was raised."

Abu Khaythama narrated to us: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salama, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: Abu Bakr used to address us and mention the beginning of the creation of man, to the extent that one of us would disgust himself, saying: "He came out of the passage of urine twice." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 200].

Al-Sha'bi said: Whoever kills two people is a tyrant (jabbar). Then he recited: ﴿Do you want to kill me as you killed a soul yesterday? You only want to be a tyrant in the land.﴾ [al-Qasas: 19]. Al-Hasan said: "How strange is the son of Adam! He washes filth with his hand twice a day, then he is arrogant! He contends with the Tyrant of the heavens." He said: Khalid ibn Khidash narrated to us: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn al-Hasan, from al-Dahhak ibn Sufyan, and he mentioned the hadith, which struck the example of this world with what comes out of the son of Adam. [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 210].

Al-Hasan said, from Yahya, from his father, who said: Indeed, the food of the son of Adam is a parable for this world, even if it is sweetened and salted.

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn 'Ali, from the descendants of 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Nothing of arrogance enters a man's heart except that it reduces his intellect to the extent of that.

Yunus ibn 'Ubayd said: There is no arrogance with prostration, and there is no hypocrisy with monotheism.

Tawus saw 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz walking with a swaggering gait, and that was before he became caliph. Tawus poked him in the side with his finger and said: "Is this the way of one who has filth in his belly?" 'Umar, as one apologizing to him, said: "O uncle, every limb of mine was beaten into this gait until I learned it."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya said: The Banu Umayya used to beat their children until they learned this gait.

Section on Strutting (al-Ikhtiyal)

From Abu Layla, from Ibn Buraydah, from his father, raised: "Whoever drags his garment out of arrogance, Allah will not look at him." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 238].

It was also narrated from Ishaq ibn Isma'il, from Sufyan, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ibn 'Umar, raised, similarly [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 239]. Muhammad ibn Bakkar narrated to us: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad narrated to us, from his father, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayra, raised: "Allah will not look on the Day of Resurrection at the one who drags his izar." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 232]. And: "While a man was strutting in his two cloaks, admiring himself, Allah caused the earth to swallow him, and he will keep sinking into it until the Day of Resurrection." [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 233].

Al-Zuhri narrated from Salim, from his father: "While a man ..." to its end. [Al-Tawadu' wal-Khumul, no. 234].

This passage contains advice that is highly beneficial, which Allah the Exalted related from Luqman the Wise, so that people may act upon it and follow it. He said: ﴿O my son, indeed it, if it should be the weight of a mustard seed﴾. That is, if the wrongdoing or the sin were the weight of a mustard seed [[addition from manuscripts T and A.]]. Some scholars permitted that the pronoun in His words ﴿indeed it﴾ be a pronoun of the matter and the story (ḍamīr al-sha'n wa'l-qiṣṣa), and on this basis they permitted the nominative case of ﴿weight﴾. The first view is the better.

As for His words ﴿Allah will bring it forth﴾, that is, Allah will produce it on the Day of Resurrection when He sets up the scales of justice, and He will recompense for it, good for good and evil for evil. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged in anything. And even if it should be the weight of a mustard seed, We would bring it forth. And sufficient are We as reckoners﴾ [al-Anbiyā’: 47]. And He the Exalted said: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it. And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 7–8]. Even if that atom were protected and hidden inside a solid rock, or absent and lost in the regions of the heavens or the earth, Allah would bring it forth, because nothing hidden is concealed from Him, and not even the weight of an atom escapes Him in the heavens or in the earth. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Subtle, Acquainted﴾, that is, Subtle in knowledge, so things are not hidden from Him however small, fine and minute they are, ﴿Acquainted﴾ with the crawling of the ant in the darkest night.

Some have claimed that what is meant by His words ﴿in a rock﴾ is a rock beneath the seven earths. This was mentioned by al-Suddi with his chain to that well-known transmission from Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud and a group of the Companions, if that is authentically established. It is also reported from 'Aṭiyyah al-'Awfi, Abu Malik, al-Thawri, al-Minhal ibn 'Amr and others. This, and Allah knows best, appears to be taken from the Isra'iliyyat (narratives derived from Jewish and Christian sources), which are neither confirmed nor denied. The apparent meaning, and Allah knows best, is that this grain, despite its smallness, even if it were inside a rock, Allah would make it appear and manifest it by His subtle knowledge, as the Imam Ahmad narrated:

Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, Ibn Lahī'ah narrated to us, Darrāj narrated to us, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who said: "If one of you were to work in a solid rock that has no door and no window, his deed would come out for the people, whatever it may be." [Musnad 3/28; al-Haythami graded it ḥasan in al-Majma' (10/225), but in its chain Ibn Lahī'ah narrates from Darrāj, and both are weak.]

Then he said: ﴿O my son, establish prayer﴾, that is, with its limits, obligations and times. ﴿And enjoin what is good and forbid what is wrong﴾, that is, according to your capacity and effort. ﴿And be patient over what has afflicted you﴾. He knew that one who enjoins good and forbids wrong will inevitably suffer harm from people, so he commanded him to be patient.

As for His words ﴿Indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination﴾, that is, indeed, patience over the harm of people is among the firm resolutions of affairs.

As for His words ﴿And do not turn your cheek [in contempt] toward people﴾, He says: do not turn your face away from people when you speak to them or they speak to you, out of contempt for them and arrogance over them. Rather, lower your side [in gentleness] and extend your face toward them, as came in the hadith: "Even if you meet your brother with a cheerful face. And beware of letting your garment trail, for it is of arrogance, and Allah does not love arrogance."

'Alī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah narrated from Ibn 'Abbās regarding His words ﴿And do not turn your cheek toward people﴾: he said, do not be arrogant so that you despise the servants of Allah and turn your face away from them when they speak to you. Similarly al-'Awfi and 'Ikrimah narrated from him.

Mālik narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam: ﴿And do not turn your cheek toward people﴾ means: do not speak while turning away. Similarly it is reported from Mujāhid, 'Ikrimah, Yazīd ibn al-Aṣamm, Abu al-Jawzā', Sa'īd ibn Jubayr, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Ibn Yazīd and others.

Ibrāhīm al-Nakha'ī said: it means affectation in speech (al-tashdīq fi'l-kalām).

The correct view is the first.

Ibn Jarīr said: The root of ṣa'ar is a disease that afflicts camels in their necks or heads, until their necks twist away from their heads. The arrogant man is likened to it. From this is the saying of 'Amr ibn Kulthūm al-Taghlibī:

"And we, when the tyrant turned his cheek [in arrogance], we straightened him from his inclination, and he straightened."

And Abu Ṭālib said in his poetry:

"And we were long ago not accepting injustice, when they bent their heads [in arrogance], we straightened them."

As for His words ﴿And do not walk upon the earth in arrogance﴾, that is, exultant, proud, haughty and obstinate. Do not do that, for Allah will hate you. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love everyone self-deluded and boastful﴾, that is, self-deluded and self-admiring, boastful over others. He the Exalted also said: ﴿And do not walk upon the earth in arrogance. Indeed, you will never tear the earth apart, nor will you reach the mountains in height﴾ [al-Isrā': 37]. The discussion of this has already preceded in its proper place.
