Ibn Kathir said, may Allah have mercy on him, in his commentary on Surah Luqman, verse 33:

He, exalted is He, says, warning people about the Day of Return and commanding them to be mindful of Him, to fear Him, and to be wary of the Day of Resurrection, on which ﴿no father will avail anything for his son﴾. That is, even if he wished to ransom him with his own self, it would not be accepted from him. Likewise, if a child wished to ransom his father with himself, it would not be accepted from him.

Then He returned to admonishing them with His words: ﴿So let not the worldly life deceive you﴾ [that is, do not let your reassurance in it distract you from the Hereafter] [[Addition from manuscripts T, F, A.]]. ﴿And let not the Deceiver deceive you about Allah﴾, meaning Satan. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, al-Dahhak and Qatadah. He deceives the son of Adam, promises him and fills him with false hopes, and none of that is real. Rather, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿He promises them and fills them with desires, but Satan promises them nothing but delusion﴾ [An-Nisa' 120].

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: 'Uzayr, peace be upon him, said: "When I saw the affliction of my people, my grief intensified, my worry increased, and my sleep became restless. So I humbled myself before my Lord, prayed and fasted. While I was in that state, humbling myself and weeping, the angel came to me. I said to him: 'Tell me, will the spirits of the truthful intercede for the wrongdoers, or will fathers intercede for their children?' He said: 'Indeed, on the Day of Resurrection there is the decisive judgment and an evident dominion, in which there is no leniency. No one speaks on that Day except by the permission of the Most Merciful. No father is taken in place of his son, no son in place of his father, no brother in place of his brother, and no slave in place of his master. No one is concerned with anyone else, and no one grieves for another's grief. No one has mercy on him; each is anxious for his own soul. No person is taken in place of another person. Each is preoccupied with his own concern, weeps over his own state, and bears his own burden, and no one else will bear his burden with him.'" Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

This is the Sunnah-based commentary on the five unseen keys (mafatih al-ghayb), the knowledge that God has reserved for Himself, so that no one knows it unless God informs him of it. The knowledge of the time of the Hour is not known to any prophet sent or any angel brought near, ﴿None but He will reveal its time﴾ [Al-A'raf: 187]. Likewise, the sending down of rain is known only to God, but when He commands it, the angels assigned to it know it, along with whomever of His creation God wills. Likewise, no one other than God knows what is in the wombs, of what He intends to create, but when He commands that it be male or female, wretched or happy, the angels assigned to that know it, along with whomever of His creation God wills. Likewise, no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, in its worldly life and its hereafter, ﴿and no soul knows in what land it will die﴾, whether in its own land or elsewhere, in whatever land of God it may be. No one has knowledge of that. This is similar to His saying, ﴿With Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but Him﴾ [Al-An'am: 59], and the Sunnah has come with naming these five "the keys of the unseen."

Imam Ahmad said: Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, Husayn ibn Waqid narrated to me, Abdullah ibn Buraydah narrated to me, I heard my father, Buraydah, say: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "Five things none knows but God, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs, and no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed, God is Knowing and Acquainted﴾" [[Al-Musnad (5/353). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/90): "The men of Ahmad are the men of the Sahih."]].

This is a hadith of sound chain, but they (the compilers of the six books) did not record it.

The hadith of Ibn Umar: Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Ibn Umar [[In T: "And al-Bukhari narrated from Abdullah ibn Umar."]], who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) [[In T: "The Prophet."]] said: "The keys of the unseen are five, none knows them but God: ﴿Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs, and no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed, God is Knowing and Acquainted﴾."

Al-Bukhari alone recorded it. He narrated it in the Book of Istisqa' (Seeking Rain) in his Sahih, from Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Firyabi, from Sufyan ibn Sa'id al-Thawri, with this chain [[Al-Musnad (2/24) and Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1035)]]. He narrated it in the Tafsir from another route, saying:

Yahya ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Umar ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn Abdullah ibn Umar narrated to me, that his father narrated to him that Abdullah ibn Umar said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The keys of the unseen are five." Then he recited: ﴿Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs﴾. He alone also narrated this [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4697)]].

Imam Ahmad also narrated it from Ghundar, from Shu'bah, from Umar ibn Muhammad, that he heard his father narrate from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "I have been given the keys of everything except five: ﴿Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs, and no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed, God is Knowing and Acquainted﴾" [[Al-Musnad (2/85).]].

[The hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, may God be pleased with him: Imam Ahmad said: Yahya narrated to us, from Shu'bah, Amr ibn Murrah narrated to me, from Abdullah ibn Salamah, who said: Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) said: "Your Prophet (ﷺ) was given the keys of everything except five: ﴿Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs, and no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed, God is Knowing and Acquainted﴾" [[In T: "And Imam Ahmad narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, who said."]] [[Added from F, A.]] [[Al-Musnad (1/386).]].

He also narrated it from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Shu'bah, from Amr ibn Murrah, with the same. He added at its end: He (Shu'bah) said: I said to him: "Did you hear it from Abdullah?" He said: "Yes, more than fifty times" [[Al-Musnad (1/438).]].

He also narrated it from Waki', from Mis'ar, from Amr ibn Murrah, with the same [[Al-Musnad (1/445).]].

This is a good chain according to the standard of the authors of the Sunan, but they did not record it.]

The hadith of Abu Hurayrah: Al-Bukhari said when commenting on this verse: Ishaq narrated to us, from Jarir, from Abu Hayyan, from Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him [[In T: "And al-Bukhari narrated."]], that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was one day sitting in public before the people, when a man came walking and said: "O Messenger of God, what is faith?" He said: "Faith is that you believe in God, His angels, His books, His messengers, and His meeting, and that you believe in the Last Resurrection." He said: "O Messenger of God, what is Islam?" He said: "Islam is that you worship God and do not associate anything with Him, establish the prayer, pay the obligatory zakat, and fast Ramadan." He said: "O Messenger of God, what is ihsan (excellence)?" He said: "Ihsan is that you worship God as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, indeed He sees you." He said: "O Messenger of God, when is the Hour?" He said: "The one asked about it does not know more than the one asking, but I will tell you about its signs: when the slave-girl gives birth to her mistress, that is one of its signs. And when the barefoot, naked ones become the leaders of the people, that is one of its signs. (It is) among five things that none knows but God: ﴿Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs﴾." Then the man left, and he said: "Bring him back to me." They went to bring him back but saw nothing. He said: "This was Gabriel, who came to teach the people their religion" [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4777).]].

Al-Bukhari also narrated it in the Book of Faith, and Muslim narrated it through several routes from Abu Hayyan, with the same [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (50) and Sahih Muslim no. (9).]]. We have discussed it at the beginning of our explanation of Sahih al-Bukhari, and we mentioned there the hadith of the Commander of the Faithful, Umar ibn al-Khattab, on this matter in full, and it is one of those narrated by Muslim alone [[Sahih Muslim no. (8).]].

The hadith of Ibn Abbas: Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Nadr narrated to us, Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, Shahr narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, narrated to us, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) sat in a gathering of his, when Gabriel came and sat before the Messenger of God (ﷺ), placing his palms on the knees of the Prophet (ﷺ), and said: "O Messenger of God, [tell me] [[Added from T, F, A, and the Musnad.]] what is Islam?" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Islam is that you submit your face to God, the Mighty and Majestic, and bear witness that there is no god but God alone, without partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger." He said: "When I do that, have I become a Muslim?" He said: "When you do that, you have become a Muslim." He said: "O Messenger of God, tell me what faith is." He said: "Faith is that you believe in God, the Last Day, the angels, the Book, and the prophets, and that you believe in death, and in life after death, and that you believe in Paradise and Hellfire, and in the reckoning and the scale, and that you believe in destiny, all of it, its good and its evil." He said: "When I do that, have I become a believer?" He said: "When you do that, you have become a believer." He said: "O Messenger of God, tell me what ihsan is." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Ihsan is that you act for God as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, indeed He sees you." He said: "O Messenger of God, tell me when the Hour is." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Glory be to God! (It is) among five things none knows but Him: ﴿Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs, and no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed, God is Knowing and Acquainted﴾. But if you wish, I will tell you about its signs, apart from that." He said: "Yes, O Messenger of God, tell me." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When you see the slave-girl give birth to her mistress, or her lord, and you see the owners of sheep competing in building, and you see the barefoot, hungry, destitute ones [become the leaders of the people], that is among the signs and portents of the Hour." He said: "O Messenger of God, who are the owners of sheep, and the barefoot, hungry, destitute ones?" He said: "The Arabs" [[Added from T, F, A, and the Musnad.]] [[Al-Musnad (1/318).]].

This is a strange (gharib) hadith, and they did not record it.

The hadith of a man from the Banu Amir: Imam Ahmad narrated: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ribi ibn Hirash, from a man from the Banu Amir, that he asked permission to enter upon the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "May I enter?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said to his servant-girl: "Go out to him, for he does not know well how to ask permission. Tell him to say: 'Peace be upon you, may I enter?'" He said: So I heard him say that, and I said: "Peace be upon you, may I enter?" He permitted me, and I entered. I said: "What did you bring us?" He said: "I have brought you nothing but good. I have come to you to tell you to worship God alone, without partner, to abandon al-Lat and al-Uzza, to pray five prayers by night and day, to fast one month of the year, to perform Hajj to the House, and to take zakat from the wealth of your rich and return it to your poor." He said: Then he said: "Is there any knowledge left that you do not know?" He said: "God, the Mighty and Majestic, has known good, and among knowledge is what none knows but God, the Mighty and Majestic: the five: ﴿Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs, and no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed, God is Knowing and Acquainted﴾." [[Al-Musnad (5/368).]] This is a sound chain.

Ibn Abi Najih narrated from Mujahid: A man from the people of the desert came and said: "My wife is pregnant, so inform me what she will bear. Our land is barren, so inform me when the rain will fall. I know when I was born, so inform me when I will die." So God, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour [and He sends down the rain]﴾, up to His saying: ﴿Indeed, God is Knowing and Acquainted﴾. Mujahid said: These are the keys of the unseen, of which God, the Exalted, said: ﴿With Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but Him﴾ [Al-An'am: 59]. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir.

Al-Sha'bi said, from Masruq, from Aishah, may God be pleased with her, that she said: "Whoever tells you that he knows what will be tomorrow has lied." Then she recited: ﴿And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow﴾ [[Tafsir al-Tabari (21/56).]].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and no soul knows in what land it will die﴾: Qatadah said: These are things God has reserved for Himself, and He has not made them known to any angel brought near or any prophet sent. ﴿Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour﴾, so no one among the people knows when the Hour will arise: in what year or what month, or by night or by day. ﴿And He sends down the rain﴾, so no one knows when the rain will fall, by night or by day. ﴿And He knows what is in the wombs﴾, so no one knows what is in the wombs, whether male or female, red or black, and what it is. ﴿And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow﴾, whether good or evil. And you, O son of Adam, do not know when you will die: perhaps you will be dead tomorrow, perhaps you will be struck tomorrow. ﴿And no soul knows in what land it will die﴾: no one among the people knows where his resting place on the earth will be, whether in the sea or on land, or in a plain or a mountain.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 31, verse 34 (part 2 of 2):

It has come in a hadith: "When God wills to take a servant's soul in a land, He makes for him a need in it." The memorizer and hadith scholar (al-Hafiz) Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said in his *al-Mu'jam al-Kabir*, in the *Musnad* (collection of hadiths arranged by narrator) of Usama ibn Zayd:

"Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, from Abu al-Malih, from Usama [[In T: "Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani narrated in his *al-Mu'jam al-Kabir*, in the Musnad of Usama."]] ibn Zayd, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: 'God does not decree a servant's death in a land without making for him a need in it.'" [[*al-Mu'jam al-Kabir* (1/178). Al-Haythami said in *al-Majma'* (7/196): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih." In it the reading is "muniyya" instead of "maytah."]]

'Abd Allah ibn al-Imam Ahmad said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us, Abu Dawud al-Hafari narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Mutar ibn 'Ukamis, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said [[In T: "'Abd Allah ibn al-Imam Ahmad narrated with his chain that the Messenger of God ﷺ said."]]: "When God decrees a servant's death in a land, He makes for him a need in it."

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in the same way in *al-Qadar*, from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri, with the same chain. [[Zawa'id al-Musnad (5/227) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2146.]] Then he said: "Hasan gharib (good, strange). Nothing is known from Mutar from the Prophet ﷺ except this hadith." And Abu Dawud narrated it in *al-Maradil*. [[I did not find it in the published *al-Maradil*.]] So God knows best.

Imam Ahmad also said: Isma'il narrated to us, Ayyub narrated to us, from Abu al-Malih ibn Usama [[In T: "And Imam Ahmad narrated."]], from Abu 'Izza [[In A: "from Abu 'Izza al-Hudhali."]], who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "When God wills to take the soul of a servant in a land, He makes for him in it, or he said: in it, a need."

This Abu 'Izza is Yasar [[In F: "Bashshar."]] ibn 'Abd Allah, and it is said: Ibn 'Abd al-Hudhali.

Al-Tirmidhi also narrated it from the hadith of Isma'il [ibn Ibrahim, who is Ibn 'Ulayya], [[Musnad (3/429) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2147.]] and said: "Sahih."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn 'Isam al-Asbahani narrated to us, al-Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il narrated to us, 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Humayd narrated to us, from Abu al-Malih, from Abu 'Izza al-Hudhali, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "When God wills to take a servant in a land, He makes for him a need toward it, and he does not stop until he reaches it." Then the Messenger of God ﷺ recited: ﴿Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs. No soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed, God is Knowing and Acquainted.﴾ [[Al-Tabarani narrated it in *al-Awsat* (no. 3248), "Majma' al-Bahrayn," by the route of 'Abbad ibn Suhayb, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Humayd, with the same wording. 'Abbad ibn Suhayb is abandoned (matruk).]]

Another hadith: The memorizer Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Ahmad ibn Thabit al-Jahdari and Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Qut'i narrated to us, both said: 'Umar ibn 'Ali narrated to us, Isma'il narrated to us, from Qays, from 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "When God wills to take a servant in a land, He makes for him a need toward it." Then al-Bazzar said: "We do not know anyone who raises this hadith except 'Umar ibn 'Ali al-Muqaddami." [[Al-Hakim narrated it in *al-Mustadrak* (1/367) by the route of Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Wahbi, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, with similar wording.]]

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Sulayman ibn Abi Masih [[In T, F, A: "Shaykh."]] narrated to me, he said: Muhammad ibn al-Hakam recited to me the verses of A'sha Hamdan:

So he took from all he had gathered only spices, on the morning of parting, along with a shroud,
And other than a breath of kindled firewood for him; and little of provision is that for one who sets out!
Do not grieve over anything, for every youth is, toward his death, a traveler on a leash,
And everyone who thinks death will miss him is deluded by follies of foolishness,
In whatever town his death is decreed, if he is not driven there willingly, he will be driven. [[In T: "I could not find these verses in what is before me of *Tarikh Dimashq* nor in the *Mukhtasar* of Ibn Manzur."]]

Ibn 'Asakir, may God have mercy on him, cited them in the biography of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, who is A'sha Hamdan. Al-Sha'bi was the husband of his sister, and he was also married to al-Sha'bi's sister. He was among those who sought knowledge and acquired understanding of religion, then he turned to the craft of poetry and became known for it.

Ibn Majah also narrated it from Ahmad ibn Thabit and 'Umar ibn Shabba, both from 'Umar ibn 'Ali [[In T, F: "'Ikrima."]], as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet ﷺ) hadith: "When the appointed term of one of you is in a land, a need brings him to it, and when he reaches the furthest point of his lifespan, God, Mighty and Majestic, takes him. The earth will say on the Day of Resurrection: 'My Lord, this is what You deposited with me.'" [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 4263. Al-Busiri said in *al-Zawa'id* (2/264): "This chain is sahih and its narrators are trustworthy." The discussion here concerns the narration of al-Bazzar, and I did not find it appropriate to place it first, since it appears this way in the manuscripts.]]

Al-Tabarani said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Abu al-Malih, from Usama, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "God does not make the death of a servant in a land except that He makes for him toward it a need." [[*al-Mu'jam al-Kabir* (1/178), already mentioned.]]

[End of the tafsir of Surah "Luqman," and praise be to God, Lord of the worlds, and He is sufficient for us and the best Disposer of affairs.] [[Added from T, F, A.]]
